body.statement: For every \(0\le\gamma\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{vac}}\), the objective \(\Psi_{\alpha,\gamma}\) is convex and lower semicontinuous on \(\Delta(\mathcal B)\), so an optimizer \(v_\gamma^\star\) exists. At the target budget \(\Gamma\), the projected interval \(I^\star\) is a nonempty closed subinterval of \([-2M,2M]\) on every assignment path and induces the schedule-independent observed-data Markov kernel \(K^\star(dI\mid O)=\delta_{I^\star(O)}(dI)\). Because \(\tau_W\in[-2M,2M]\) and \(\lvert\Pi_M(x)-\tau_W\rvert\le\lvert x-\tau_W\rvert\), it satisfies \(\inf_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}}P^{K^\star}_{\mathcal D,Y}(\tau_W\in I^\star)\ge1-\alpha\). Its worst-case expected length is at most \(2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\): the projected branch has length at most \(2\Psi_\alpha(v^\star)\), the full-space branch has length \(4M\), and the empty-intersection fallback event has probability zero.
body.justification: This is the constructive half of the borrowing frontier and gives finite-sample design-based coverage using average rather than worst-path information.
body.gap: LeeWason2020 compares all-control and concurrent-only analyses in a two-stage adding-arm platform under parametric linear and step trends, LiZhao2026 proves asymptotic Wald coverage for centered adaptive AIPW, SawadaNomuraShinozaki2026 controls an estimated external-control bias cap, ChenLiZhangYe2025 Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and an attaining upper construction for a Gaussian RCT--observational model under a scalar confounding-bias bound, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift studies fixed-effect, mixed-effect, and spline time adjustment through simulated type-I error and power. None supplies an everywhere-nonempty uniform fixed-schedule randomization interval over a TV drift class with an assignment-law-averaged platform-borrowing criterion.
